small_guidance:
- The conv3d kernel dominates runtime (output 128×16×14×30×30 with 3×3×3×3 reduction). Tile multiple OC together per program (BLOCK_OC=4 or 8) and reuse the same x loads across OC; sweep BLOCK_W in {16,32,64} and num_warps in {2,4,8}, num_stages in {2,3,4} via `triton.autotune`.
- Hoist the `((n*IC+ic)*ID + id_)*IH*IW` base index out of the kh/kw loops and only add `kh*IW + kw` inside; this removes redundant multiplies inside the innermost static loop.
- In `fused_norm_clamp_max_kernel`, BLOCK_C=16 with BLOCK_S=256 and num_warps=4 should improve occupancy; also fuse the stats pass into the same kernel as a two-pass persistent kernel per (N) tiling over S to skip the extra mean/invstd round trip.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite conv3d as an implicit-GEMM: one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial-tile), with GEMM-K = IC*KT*KH*KW. Use `tl.dot` with BLOCK_M (OC) = 16/32, BLOCK_N (spatial) = 32/64, BLOCK_K = 32, channels-last on input so the K-axis is contiguous. This will be far faster than the current scalar-accumulate loop over IC×KT×KH×KW.
- Fuse the conv epilogue with `* multiplier`: load the per-OC multiplier once into registers and apply it before writeback. This eliminates a full pass over the (N,OC,OD,OH,OW)=128·16·14·30·30 tensor.
- Replace the two-kernel stats+apply with a single persistent per-(N,C) kernel: each program owns one (n,c) row of S=12600 elements, computes Welford stats in registers, then a second pass over the same row applies (norm, clamp, ×mult) and atomically reduces into a per-(n, s) max output — or alternatively keep a per-(n) program that holds all C=16 channels resident across the spatial tile so the max reduction is intra-register with no atomics.
